newsitem.title: USA: Korea talks adjourn, to resume Friday.
newsitem.headline: Korea talks adjourn, to resume Friday.

text.p: Negotiations on bringing North Korea into proposed four-party talks on a lasting peace on the Korean peninsula were adjourned on Wednesday and will resume on Friday, the chief U.S. negotiator said.

Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Charles Kartman told reporters after a day of talks: "I don't have anything conclusive to tell you. We made some encouraging progress. There's still more to be done. We'll meet again on Friday."
The New York talks included delegations from the United States, North Korea and South Korea.
North Korea's negotiator Kim Gye Gwan told reporters there had been "encouraging progress" but said sometimes it took time to conclude such deliberations.

Earlier U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and the State Department spokesman had reported early progress in the talks and Albright indicated North Korea was on the verge of agreeing to participate in the four-party talks, which would also involve China.
Washington proposed the four-party talks jointly with South Korea a year ago to finally close the books on the 1950-53 Korean War by replacing the fraying armistice with a peace treaty.
